# Components and style

Style goes through the project tokens, never through hand-written values. A component without its five states is not finished.

Marker after the identifier: a tool name = tooled constraint (the build or the commit fails); `guidance` = rule of conduct checked in review.

## Base rules

### Rules

- **CORE-010** · guidance — A component that can be loading, empty or failing renders an explicit state for each of the three, and never returns `null` instead.
  Why: These three states are the ones an agent left alone forgets; a blank screen is the most expensive bug to diagnose.
- **CORE-011** · guidance — Every interactive component handles the disabled state and shows a visible `:focus-visible` ring.
  Why: With loading, empty and error, these are the five states that make a component finished.
- **CORE-012** · guidance — A presentational component receives its data through props and never calls the network or a query hook itself.
  Why: A component that fetches cannot be reused, previewed or tested without a server.
- **CORE-013** · guidance — One file exports one component; its variants live in the same file through `cva`, never as copied files.
  Why: A copied variant drifts from the original at the first change.
- **CORE-014** · `typescript` — Props are typed explicitly and `any` never appears, in a component or in a hook.
  Why: The prop types are the contract other developers and the agent read first.
- **CORE-015** · `eslint` — A list renders a stable business key, never the array index.
  Why: An index key corrupts local state as soon as the list is sorted or filtered.
- **CORE-016** · guidance — Business logic longer than one ternary lives in a hook or a plain function, never inline in JSX.
  Why: JSX describes what is displayed; logic buried in it is untestable.
- **CORE-017** · guidance — `useEffect` is used only to synchronise with something outside React; anything derivable is computed during render.
  Why: Effects that recompute state are the main source of extra renders and stale values.
- **CORE-020** · `stylelint` — Colours, spacing, radii and font sizes come from the project tokens; no raw hex, rgb or px value appears in a component.
  Why: A value written by hand escapes the theme, the dark mode and any later change of brand.
- **CORE-021** · `eslint` — Tailwind arbitrary values (`p-[13px]`, `text-[#3a5bd9]`) are forbidden.
  Why: They are the same hand-written value, hidden inside a class name.
- **CORE-022** · `stylelint` — Colours are used through their semantic token (`--color-surface`, `--color-destructive`), never through a palette shade.
  Why: A semantic name survives a palette change; `blue-600` does not.
- **CORE-023** · guidance — The dark theme redefines the same tokens; no component branches on the active theme.
  Why: A component that knows about the theme has to be changed twice for every visual change.
- **CORE-024** · `stylelint` — Spacing uses the scale built on the base step; no intermediate value is introduced.
  Why: A single rhythm is what makes screens written by different hands look like one product.
- **CORE-025** · `stylelint` — Text sizes come from the modular scale tokens, and only the weights listed in the visual contract are used.
  Why: Two extra sizes and one extra weight are enough to make a typography look accidental.
- **CORE-026** · `stylelint` — `!important` never appears in the project stylesheets.
  Why: It is the sign of a specificity problem that the next developer will have to solve twice.
- **CORE-027** · guidance — A new token is added to the token file and to both themes in the same change, never inline in a component.
  Why: The token file is the only readable inventory of the visual language.

### Anti-patterns

- **CORE-AP-010** · guidance — Returning `null` while data is loading, leaving the user in front of a blank area.
  Why: The user cannot tell a slow screen from a broken one.
  Instead: Render the skeleton or the spinner of the design system, sized like the final content.
- **CORE-AP-011** · `jsx-a11y` — A `<div onClick>` used as a button.
  Why: It is unreachable by keyboard and invisible to assistive technology.
  Instead: Use a `<button>`, styled with the tokens of the design system.
- **CORE-AP-020** · `stylelint` — A colour picked from a mockup and pasted into a class for one screen.
  Why: It works today and breaks the dark theme, the contrast check and the next redesign.
  Instead: Reuse the closest semantic token, or add one to the token file if the meaning is new.

## Profile `spa-feature`

Vite single-page application, one directory per use case, imports flowing strictly downwards.

### Visual contract

| Token | Value |
|---|---|
| Typography | system-ui, sans-serif · system-ui, sans-serif · ui-monospace, monospace |
| Modular scale | 1.125 |
| Allowed weights | 400, 500, 600 |
| Line length | 80ch |
| Spacing step | 4px |
| Radius | 4px |

**Semantic colours**

| Token | Light | Dark |
|---|---|---|
| `--color-background` | `#ffffff` | `#0d1117` |
| `--color-surface` | `#f2f4f7` | `#151b23` |
| `--color-text` | `#0f172a` | `#e6e9ee` |
| `--color-muted` | `#556070` | `#9aa4b2` |
| `--color-border` | `#cfd5dd` | `#262d37` |
| `--color-primary` | `#1f5f9e` | `#78b3e8` |
| `--color-primary-foreground` | `#ffffff` | `#0d1117` |
| `--color-destructive` | `#a32019` | `#f0a19a` |
| `--color-success` | `#186b45` | `#79cfa4` |

### Rules

- **SPA-010** · guidance — A component used by two features moves to `shared/ui` in its own commit, stripped of business vocabulary.
  Why: Promoting a component is a decision; copying it is how a design system dies.
